items.title: How Does Local AI Reduce Vendor Dependency?
items.summary:
Local AI gives you something every developer wants more of: control.

In this short, Keiji Kamigusa explains how running AI models on your own Mac can reduce dependency on outside vendors, cloud APIs, shifting pricing, rate limits, outages, and black-box systems.

Instead of building everything around one provider’s platform, you can create AI apps that run locally, protect your data, and stay flexible as the ecosystem changes.

Build Applications with Local AI Models on a Mac shows you how to start building that kind of independence for real: private chatbots, RAG apps, voice tools, and practical AI workflows you can run on your own machine.

If you want AI that works for you, not just through someone else’s API, this is the book to check out.

Learn more: https://hubs.la/Q04mY6wQ0

#LocalAI #PrivateAI #OpenSourceAI #MacAI #AppleSilicon #Ollama #AIEngineering #RAG #AIApps #ManningBooks

items.title: Next-Gen Self-Evolving AI Agents (ATDP)
items.summary:
AI Agents That Rewrite Themselves, without any humans.

Self-evolving agents require an enterprise-grade agentic data proxy that captures ATDP trajectories from real production workloads across models, tools, memory systems, retrieval systems, and human-feedback
channels.

Self-evolving agents require a unified agent evolution control plane that decides when, where, and how agent behavior should change. Self-evolution should not be equated with blindly updating model weights.

A deployed agent is a composite policy consisting of a base LLM, an in-context harness, memory, tools, and guardrails; different failures require different intervention surfaces.

items.title: How to "Vibe Direct" Short Films
items.summary:
We've gone from vibe coding to vibe DIRECTING.

Instead of prompting individual clips and stitching everything together afterward, you can now direct an entire video through conversation.

I used @openart_ai Director to create my own horror movie trailer by describing the story, characters, pacing, visuals, and voice performances, then refining everything through chat.

It can generate up to 5 minutes (NOT seconds!) of continuous video while keeping the characters, voices, and story consistent the whole way through.

If you’re interested in trying your hand at vibe directing, head to OpenArt.ai to get started.

#AI #genAI #aivideo #AIart

items.title: A decade of quantum on the cloud
items.summary:
Visit The Coherence Times podcast page to get more AI content → https://www.ibm.com/think/podcasts/the-coherence-times

It was almost exactly ten years ago, on May 4, 2026, that IBM put the first quantum computer on the cloud. This was a seminal moment in computing history. For the first time, anyone could run quantum circuits on a real quantum computer from anywhere with an internet connection. That single act took quantum computers out of the research lab, and put them in the hands of a global community of researchers, developers, students, and enthusiasts. In this week’s episode of The Coherence Times, we sit down with IBM Quantum CTO of Quantum-Centric Supercomputing Jerry Chow and Oak Ridge National Laboratory Quantum Science Center Director Travis Humble to discuss that moment in history, and the decade of exploration and ecosystem development it inspired.

Run your first quantum circuit on IBM Quantum Platform → https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com
The opinions expressed in this podcast are solely those of the participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of IBM or any other organization or entity.

items.title: The AI Threat Almost No One Is Working On (with Benjamin Todd)
items.summary:
#AIcareers #AISafety #80000Hours

Benjamin Todd, co-founder and President of 80,000 Hours and author of the new Penguin Random House book 80,000 Hours: How to Have a Fulfilling Career That Does Good, joins @JonKrohnLearns for a major update on career strategy in the AI era, his first appearance since before ChatGPT existed. Ben explains why “follow your passion” is backwards and why rare, valuable skills used to help others are what actually generate lasting fulfillment, the ABZ framework for planning under deep uncertainty, why the only durable move is to keep shifting onto whatever bottleneck AI can’t yet clear, and how a human-level digital worker becomes superhuman almost immediately. He and Jon also map the risk landscape, power-seeking AI, extreme power concentration, engineered pandemics, gradual disempowerment, and S-risks, before landing on a hopeful, actionable note: your career is a bigger lever than ever.

This episode is brought to you by: 
• Anthropic: https://claude.ai/superdata
• Acceldata: https://www.acceldata.io
• Gurobi: https://www.superdatascience.com/gurobi

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:06:44) The ABZ framework for career planning under deep uncertainty
• (00:14:30) Why “follow your passion” is backwards and what builds fulfillment instead
• (00:21:33) The moving bottleneck: how to stay valuable as AI keeps improving
• (00:33:17) Why a human-level digital worker becomes superhuman almost immediately
• (00:51:19) Power-seeking AI and extreme power concentration
• (01:16:11) Why your career is a bigger lever than ever
